newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK interbank rates, govt paper yields slightly up.
newsitem.headline: HK interbank rates, govt paper yields slightly up.

text.p: Hong Kong interbank market rates moved slightly higher on Monday in the wake of last week's numerous new share issues, dealers said.
Overnight money rose to 5-9/16 1/2 percent from 5-1/2 7/16 at Friday midday. Three-month rate was at 5-9/16 1/2 percent versus 5-1/2, a local bank dealer said.
"Short-term money remains tight beacuse of four IPOs (initial public offerings) last week," he said.
Hong Kong government paper yields were also up following moves by U.S. Treasuries, a dealer with a Japanese bank said.

Yields for seven-year Exchange Fund notes rose to 7.07 percent from 7.04 at Friday's midsession, five-year notes ended at 6.73 percent against 6.70 and three-year stood at 6.16 percent versus 6.11 percent.
The short-dated one-week bill was at 4.96 percent versus 4.90 at Friday's midday.
